name: SWOT Analysis
use_case: A structured framework for evaluating an organization, project, or initiative across four quadrants: internal Strengths and Weaknesses, and external Opportunities and Threats. Best used early in strategic planning when the team needs to surface assumptions and align on the competitive landscape before committing to a direction.
strengths: simple to facilitate in a 1–2 hour workshop
outputs are immediately actionable as discussion fuel
low complexity barrier — works with mixed-experience groups
weaknesses: can be superficial without rigorous evidence behind each cell
easily becomes a wishlist rather than an analysis
use_cases: A school leadership team drafting its improvement plan wants teachers and parents to take honest stock of where the school stands before it picks its priorities.
A university department reviewing a degree programme wants students and faculty to say what works, what is missing, and which outside changes could affect it.
A public agency starting its multi-year plan needs staff from different units to agree on what the organisation does well, where it falls short, and what around it could help or hurt.
At a mid-point review, a project team suspects its original assumptions about its own capabilities and its surroundings no longer hold and wants to re-examine them together.
